AID FOR DELIVERY RIDERS

Up to 21,127 delivery riders are set to receive financial assistance today, March 26, at Kartilya ng Katipunan in Manila.

In coordination with the Manila Department of Social Welfare and Development and the Manila Traffic and Parking Bureau, each qualified beneficiary will receive ₱5,000 from the Department of Social Welfare and Development under its Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situations (AICS) program, in partnership with the Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board.

📸 The STAR/Edd Gumban

data.raw_text:
During severe flooding caused by Typhoon Tino in the Philippines, a 15 year old boy showed extraordinary courage by rescuing more than 50 people trapped in rising waters. As conditions became dangerous, many residents struggled to reach safety.

Despite the risk, the teenager used his strength and determination to help others. Moving through flooded areas, he guided people to safer locations and ensured that those in danger were not left behind. His actions required both physical effort and quick decision making.

Flood situations can be extremely unpredictable. Strong currents, hidden obstacles, and limited visibility make rescue efforts difficult even for trained responders. Yet, he stepped forward without hesitation, driven by a desire to protect others.

His bravery did not go unnoticed. In recognition of his efforts, he was later awarded a full scholarship, giving him the opportunity to continue his education and build a brighter future.

This story highlights how courage can come from unexpected places. It shows that even at a young age, individuals can make a powerful difference in critical moments.

His actions serve as a reminder that helping others during difficult times can create lasting impact and inspire communities to come together with strength and unity.

data.raw_text:
"It's not like we Filipinos are so smart that we're gonna find a new solution to this problem." This isn't a new problem. Cities all over the world — from Taipei to Singapore to Bangkok — have faced these same problems and were able to figure it out. Wider sidewalks. Protected lanes. Pedestrians and cyclists sharing space safely, away from traffic.

And yet on EDSA — no proper sidewalks. Bike lanes taken over by motorcycles. Cyclists too scared to ride. Commuters forced to walk on the carriageway just to get from one mode of transport to another.

We don't need to reinvent anything. We just need to copy what works. And @DPWHph Secretary Vince Dizon is finally making it happen.
